Without knowing more about the C8, without any personal knowledge or experience, I can't really offer an opinion.

Then, there's the stats and performance numbers. Those are lovely metrics and can tell you a lot about a car, but there's a big difference between what the performance specs say and what happens on the asphalt.

That said, the Corvette has always been a good bargain for a performance car. It's an inexpensive way to get a bunch of ponies and performance. It's a lot easier to get a C8 than it is to get a GT3 RS. It's a lot less expensive and they make a shitload more of them.

You don't buy a GT3 RS to race a Corvette. You buy a GT3 RS to drive the best 911 on the market. You buy a GT3 RS because you love Porsche. You buy a Corvette because you want inexpensive power options and don't need the Porsche-experience.
